findings.description: The security group allows inbound TCP/22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH on the instance to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or exploit attempts.
The egress rule permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, allowing a compromised instance unrestricted outbound connectivity for data exfiltration or C2 traffic.

The user_data script exports AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY in plaintext; EC2 user data is retrievable via the instance metadata service and stored unencrypted, leaking long-lived AWS credentials.
No metadata_options block sets http_tokens = "required", so the instance allows IMDSv1, making instance credentials reachable through SSRF attacks on the public web server.
The instance does not define root_block_device with encrypted = true, so the root EBS volume may store data unencrypted at rest.
The EBS volume is created without encrypted = true and no KMS key, leaving attached data unencrypted at rest.
The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted volume, so the backup data is also stored unencrypted and could be exposed if shared or copied.
The bucket storing VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration (aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration), so sensitive network telemetry may be stored unencrypted.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or ACL/policy controls are defined for the flow log bucket, risking public exposure of network traffic logs.

findings.issue_category: Force destroy enabled on log bucket
findings.description: force_destroy = true allows the audit/flow-log bucket and all its objects to be deleted without safeguards, enabling destruction of security evidence.
No versioning configuration is present, so flow log objects can be overwritten or deleted irrecoverably, weakening log integrity.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance in this subnet to receive a public IP, directly exposing workloads to the internet.
